articles.title: The rise of Edwin Sifuna: from ODM secretary-general to opposition presidential contender
articles.summary: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has moved from running ODM's party machinery to leading a new political movement backed for the 2027 presidential race.
articles.body:
Edwin Sifuna, a lawyer, was named secretary-general of the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) on 23 February 2018, replacing Ababu Namwamba. In August 2022 he won the Nairobi Senate seat, defeating Bishop Margaret Wanjiru. 

His profile grew most after the death of ODM leader Raila Odinga and ODM's cooperation deal with President William Ruto's government. Sifuna became the face of resistance inside the party by openly criticising the agreement with the government and insisting ODM should remain a full opposition party. 
nation

That stance cost him his party post. The Registrar of Political Parties approved his removal as secretary-general, saying it followed the Political Parties Act and ODM's constitution. One account lists his time in the post as running until 9 July 2026. 

Outside the party, support was already forming. Linda Mwananchi leaders from Western Kenya announced plans for a new party and said they would put Sifuna forward for president. The Linda Mwananchi Movement later endorsed him as its presidential candidate after a retreat attended by several senior figures. 

The movement has faced legal hurdles. The Political Parties Disputes Tribunal set aside the Registrar's August 7 refusal to reserve the name, and in a letter dated October 1, 2026 the Registrar approved the application. The name is reserved for 90 days, and the movement must use that window to become an actual political organisation. Rival applications for similar names have also emerged. 

This week he has also taken on the government directly. He demanded in the Senate that Parliament be shown the agreement behind the proposed Dangote refinery in Lamu, and later cited Article 35 of the Constitution on access to information. President Ruto accused him of seeking the document outside Parliament, called him an extortionist, and said it should be requested through parliamentary procedures. On October 3 at a burial in Kirinyaga, Sifuna asked Mt Kenya residents to help settle who should carry the opposition ticket in 2027. 
Sifuna warns against secretive deals amid Dangote Oil Refinery row - People Daily +2

Whether the rise continues depends on registration deadlines and on whether the opposition agrees on a single candidate.

Sources: Nation, Citizen Digital, People Daily, Wikipedia.

articles.title: Gachagua says he is now aiming for State House in 2027, after earlier talk of backing Ruto to 2032
articles.summary: A headline circulating online quotes Rigathi Gachagua saying he once pledged to back President Ruto until 2032 but now expects to become president in 2027.
articles.body:
A statement attributed to former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua is drawing attention online. According to a headline circulating on social media, he said he had promised to support President William Ruto until 2032 but now expects to be president in 2027.

The remark appears alongside a video on Gachagua's official Facebook page, captioned "Through Partnership with the Diaspora, we shall bridge the gap on employment." The caption points to the diaspora and jobs as themes of the event. The exact wording of the quote, and where and when it was said, should be confirmed from the original video.

Gachagua announced on September 14, 2025, in Nyeri that he would run for president in 2027. By January 2026, as Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader, he was touring the Mt Kenya region and repeating that Ruto should serve only one term. In July 2026 he also said he would step aside for another candidate if that was what it took to unite the opposition and remove Ruto. 
'No lies, no false promises': Gachagua launches bid to unseat Ruto +2

The 2032 claim has been disputed before. During the 2022 campaign, Gachagua said his arrangement with Ruto was a five-year performance contract and that he had not agreed to back Ruto after his ten-year term. Later, a Mt Kenya politician, Mr Wamumbi, said he had personally advised Gachagua to submit to Ruto's presidency until 2032 before pursuing his own ambitions. 
peopledaily
nation

Allies of President Ruto have consistently downplayed opposition unification efforts, expressing confidence in the government's record and its prospects in 2027. 
peopledaily

Source: Gachagua's official Facebook page and published reports.

articles.title: KICC lit up in tribute to Raila Odinga as ODM opens "Mwezi wa Baba"
articles.summary: The Kenyatta International Convention Centre in Nairobi glowed with a tribute to the late former Prime Minister on Friday night, as ODM began a month of remembrance events.
articles.body:
Nairobi's Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) became a canvas for a light display honouring the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga on Friday evening, while supporters in other parts of the country held remembrance events of their own.

The projection formed part of a countrywide candle-lighting led by the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), which kicked off its October programme, named "Mwezi wa Baba", in memory of Raila, widely known as Baba.

Clips posted on ODM's official X account showed a glowing image of Raila circling the landmark tower, with the words "Baba Raila Odinga" displayed near the top of the building.

Source: videos shared on ODM's official X account.
